thermite3-migrate's 'edits' mode exits 0 on source that does not parse. It prints items=N errors=M to stderr and emits edits for the items that DID parse; 'to-v3' on the same input exits 3. Verified directly on a two-item fragment with one malformed item: edits exit 0, errors=1, 4 edits printed; to-v3 exit 3. Any write path built on 'edits' must gate on the errors= count and not on the exit status, or it half-migrates a file the tool actually declined - the same class of silent skip a round-trip cannot see, running in the opposite direction. The .th corpus path is unaffected because it uses to-v3.

RFC-6's stated replacement for the round-trip is implemented and passes across the whole corpus. One structural-fingerprint program compiles against either thermite-syntax unchanged, because Contract { req, ens, fx } has the same shape on both sides of the rename, so the v2 front end reads the unmigrated file and the v3 front end reads the migrated one and the fingerprints are compared directly. It prints item names, clause expression text, @bv width and nowrap, and the effect row, and deliberately omits keyword spellings, which are what is supposed to change. Result over 67 files: 66 AST-identical, 0 differing, 1 declined by BOTH parsers (recover_per_item.th, by design), 0 parsing on one side only. First run reported 7 files differing; every difference was a BvTag span.start leaking through the Debug format, which must move because the migrated source is longer. Spans are positional, not semantic, and are now excluded - a fingerprint that includes a byte offset cannot distinguish a rename from a regression.

RFC-6's figure of 1527 clause sites in Rust literals is an undercount, and the undercount is structural rather than arithmetic. coverage.py decides whether a literal is a CANDIDATE before it ever runs the front end, with re.search(r'(^|'+re.escape(sep)+r')\s*(pub\s+)?(spec\s+)?(fn|struct|enum|protocol|lemma|prop|spec)\s', body). Two shapes fail that test and are therefore never looked at, so they appear in no count - not as migrated, not as declined. First, a literal opening with an attribute: '#[boundary("ext::e")] fn bnd(...)' and '#[slag(...)] fn vendored(...)' put a token before the declaration (25 of them). Second, and larger, a plain literal written across several source lines with backslash continuations holds REAL newlines, while sep for a plain literal is the two-character escape, so a fn on the literal's second line is preceded by neither ^ nor that escape (64 of them). Measured on the pin: 87 literals, 353 clause sites, 41 files, all of which migrate CLEAN when handed to the front end. True total is 1880 rather than 1527. This is the enumerate-your-declines discipline defeated one stage earlier: coverage.py lists every decline honestly, and a filter that runs before the decline logic makes the report silent about a whole population. It is what breaks divergence_adt_parse, divergence_intlit_spec_fn_ret and divergence_spec_call_param_cast under the new front end.

A Rust rewriter's spans are BYTE offsets; a Python driver's string indices are CHARACTER indices, and unescape.py's offset map is character-based. Mixing them silently corrupts text, and it only shows where non-ASCII precedes a clause keyword - which in this codebase means anywhere the house-style em dash appears in a comment. In forge/src/contract_tv.rs the third item's edits landed two bytes late and wrote 're! pure', 'requires.len() > 0' and 'enensuresesult == t.byte_at(0)' into the literal. The corruption survived every counter: the tool reported 530 migrated, 1880 sites, 1396 of 1396 accounted for, 0 refused. What caught it was parsing the migrated literal with the NEW front end and finding it declined - the AST comparison, not the accounting. Fix is a byte-offset-to-character-index map applied before any use of an edit, with a refusal path for an offset that is not on a character boundary. The .th and JSON paths are unaffected because they use to-v3, where the splice happens inside Rust and stays in bytes throughout. Generalizes: when a tool hands you offsets, the units are part of the contract, and a counter that says 'all accounted for' is counting its own bookkeeping rather than the output.

The literal scanner every measurement of the Rust-literal population depends on desynchronizes on Rust lifetimes. thermite-migrate.py::_rust_literals treats every apostrophe as opening a char literal and scans to the next one; Rust also spells lifetimes with a single quote - &'static, Foo<'_>, impl<'a> - and those have no partner, so the scan runs to whatever apostrophe comes next and every string literal in between is never yielded. It is silent in the strongest sense: those literals are neither migrated nor declined, they are invisible, and no counter moves. thermite-spec/src/s2_recon.rs has &'static at line 71; the scanner yields 31 literals and stops at line 1651 of a 2000-line file. Measured across the pin: 66 literals carrying 273 clause sites in 15 files, all of which migrate clean once the scanner is fixed. A char literal is recognised by requiring the quoted run to CLOSE ('a', '\n', '\u{1F600}'); anything else is a lifetime and consumes only the tick, so the scanner stays in sync. Running total for the Rust-literal population is now 2153 clause sites against RFC-6's published 1527.

A defect in RFC-6's own implementation on anchor/implementation, found by probing rather than reading: addresses_of emits an address that resolve rejects. validate_segments was migrated to the allowlist {measures, proof, ensures, requires, keeps} and emit_loop_addresses was migrated for invariants (inv#N -> keeps#N) but NOT for the loop measure, which still formats {loop_addr}.dec. So on conformance/sum.th the emitter produces sum.loop#1.dec and resolve returns Malformed("sum.loop#1.dec"), while sum.loop#1.measures returns NotFound - the loop measure is unaddressable in either spelling, and address.rs's own module doc says resolution is bidirectional and never panics. Every other emitted address round-trips. The fix is one line, format!("{loop_addr}.measures"), after which all seven addresses on sum.th resolve and the v2 spelling is correctly Malformed. This is why RFC-6's compiler-change table undercounts address.rs: it lists validate_segments at :331 and :347 as 2 lines, and the emitter at :286 is a third site.

Second defect of the same class on anchor/implementation, and it is the one that shows the pattern. parse_clause_selector in parser.rs stored the clause family as "ens"/"req"/"inv" while its own doc comment had been half-migrated to 'ensures#k / req / keeps#k'. That string becomes an ADDRESS SEGMENT - a proof obligation is addressed f.proof.<family>#k - so addresses_of emitted f.proof.ens#2 and f.proof.ens#2.?p3, both of which the same crate's resolve rejects as Malformed under the migrated validate_segments allowlist. Verified by probe, not by reading. Together with the loop measure at address.rs:286 this is a consistent shape: RFC-6's rename was applied to the LEXER and to the VALIDATOR, and missed the three places the front end CONSTRUCTS a clause name as data - format!("{loop_addr}.dec"), the ClauseSelector family strings, and their diagnostics. A rename measured as 'keyword_kind entries: 5' does not see those, because they are not keywords, they are strings that have to agree with keywords. Fixes are three lines plus their doc comments. After them thermite-syntax, thermite-spec and thermite-lower are 332 passed, 0 failed.

A package-scoped test run and a workspace test run do not cover the same tests, and the difference hid seven failures. cargo test -p thermite-syntax builds that crate with its DEFAULT features, so bv is off and thermite-syntax/tests/bv_tag_parse.rs runs 3 tests; the whole mod plumbing_present is #[cfg(feature = "bv")]. Under cargo test --workspace, feature unification turns bv on because another member depends on thermite-syntax with features = ["bv"], the same module compiles, and it runs 10. So an earlier '332 passed, 0 failed' across thermite-syntax, thermite-spec and thermite-lower was a real result about a smaller set of tests than it sounded like, and the bv-tagged fixtures it did not run were still in v2. Same lesson as the corpus tooling, one level up: the number is about what the command reached, and for cargo that is decided by feature resolution rather than by the package list. Post-migration test evidence for this RFC has to come from a workspace run.

The test suite ran, and it is scored against a control rather than against zero. Full cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast on the migrated tree AND on a git archive export of 84d276e7, same machine, same Verus 0.2026.05.24.ecee80a on PATH. Baseline: 1395 passed, 49 unique failing tests - the pin does NOT have a green suite in this environment, because lean/.lake/packages/mathlib is an unresolvable checkout so every Mathlib-backed reconstruction fails, and cadical is absent so the EPR route reports EprSolverUnavailable. Migrated at that point: 1378 passed, 66 unique failing. Set difference gives 18 tests failing ONLY after migration, in five groups, every one a downstream artifact that pins source text or a clause spelling rather than anything about meaning: 8 shelling out to forge over fixtures assembled by concat! or format! that no single literal covers; 4 in goal_repl pinning clause spans and proof-for addresses; committed_skill_is_fresh; a kernel-image boundary contract digest that must be re-pinned because the contract text moved; and editor content pins. All but the digest are now migrated. Reporting a bare pass count here would have been dishonest in both directions - it would have charged 49 environmental failures to the rename, and hidden the 18 real ones among them.

The clause-name-as-data population is larger than the two defects already recorded, and it is a third migration population in its own right. A clause name is used as an ADDRESS SEGMENT in three ways: constructed at run time (format!("{}.loop#{}.inv#{}") in contract_tv.rs:357, format!("{}.req") at :227, format!("{}.ens#{}") at :240), pinned in test expectations (goal_repl.rs, proof_fill.rs, contract_tv_conformance.rs, goal_repl.rs tests), and emitted in user-facing help (cli.rs:1561 'forge edit requires a semantic <addr> (e.g. binary_search.loop#1.inv#2)'). None of these is a keyword, so none is visible to a rename scoped by keyword_kind; all of them have to agree with validate_segments or the address does not resolve. 11 files carried them. This is why the anchor's own test suite kept failing after the corpus and every string literal were migrated: the surface moved, and the places that SPELL the surface as data did not.

Re-pinned the frozen kernel source-contract digest rather than exempting the kernel corpus from the migration. thermite-kernel/src/registry.rs pins sha256 over format!("{:#?}", contract) for kernel::clock::read@v1; that Debug rendering carries clause SPANS, so migrating conformance/bootable_kernel.th moves the digest from 2a1b32cc... to 3f525f14... even though nothing about the contract's meaning changes. Re-pinned with a dated comment keeping the prior value, the convention used for audited-content-sha256 elsewhere in this tree. This is worth a maintainer's explicit attention rather than being buried in a 253-file diff: the digest exists to detect contract drift, so a migration that legitimately moves it is also a migration that asks reviewers to accept a new trust anchor on the author's word. The evidence offered for that acceptance is the structural fingerprint - item names, clause expression text, @bv tags and effect row are byte-identical across the two front ends for all 66 parsing corpus files - which is a stronger statement than the digest itself makes, because the digest is over a rendering that includes byte offsets.

Final state on anchor/implementation: 253 files changed, 2172 insertions, 1998 deletions - 67 .th, 159 .rs, 22 .json, 4 .fixture, 1 .md. Evidence, each reproducible: (1) forge check --level l3 --json on RFC-6's six files, baseline from a git archive of 84d276e7, Verus 0.2026.05.24.ecee80a - exit 0/0/0/0/1/0 both directions, 18 items at L3 both directions, every item identical on the oracle subset, map_kv.th reproducing EnsIsTrivial on demo and WeakContract on build_one and lookup_absent. (2) The AST comparison RFC-6 asks for, one fingerprint program compiled against both front ends: 66 of 67 corpus files byte-identical structurally, 1 declined by both (recover_per_item.th, by design); 596 rewritten Rust literals AST-identical, 857 declined literals byte-identical, 0 files whose literal count changed, 0 problems. (3) cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast on the migrated tree and on the pin, same machine, same Verus: 1396 passed / 48 failed migrated against 1395 / 49 baseline, and the set difference of failing test NAMES is EMPTY - every remaining failure also fails at the pin, from an unresolvable lean/.lake mathlib checkout and an absent cadical. One test that fails at the pin now passes. (4) Goldens needed no regeneration, which is RFC-6's 'lowering becomes identity' claim holding: Verus already spells requires/ensures, and tests/golden/ is untouched by the migration.
